Tipperary County Council is pleased to announce 
that a contract has been awarded to Wills Bros 
Ltd for the construction of the R498 Latteragh 
Realignment Scheme.  The scheme involves the 
improvement of a 4.3km section of the existing 
R498 Regional Road between Nenagh and 
Thurles, at Latteragh, approximately 7km south-
east of the M7 Nenagh Bypass. RPS Group 
Consultants were employed to carry out the 
detailed design and will supervise the works on

behalf of Tipperary County Council.  This scheme 
represents an investment of approximately €35m 
which is being provided to Tipperary County 
Council by the Department of Transport. The 
new road cross-section will be a single carriageway 
with a shared footway/cycle track along the length 
of the scheme. The existing three junctions will 
also be improved as part of the scheme.   
 
Access to all properties will be maintained 
throughout the 18-month period of the works.  
Works of this nature will cause some disruption, 
but it is the intention of Tipperary County Council 
and our contractor to minimise this as far as 
possible.  
 
Liam Brett, Director of Services, Tipperary 
County Council, stated that “this is a significant 
scheme and investment in roads infrastructure in 
Tipperary which will bring safety, economic, and 
environmental benefits with enhanced linkage 
between the north and south of the county.  The 
scheme supports government plans and policies in 
relation to transport and spatial development in 
the Mid-West Region”. 
Sinead Carr, Chief Executive, Tipperary County 
Council, signed the contract and said “the Council 
has been working closely with the Department of 
Transport to bring this project to construction.  I 
am delighted that the Council has now awarded 
this contract and I look forward to works 
commencing in the near future”.    
 
John Carroll MCC, Cathaoirleach of Tipperary 
County Council stated that “the road re-alignment 
scheme at Latteragh is a significant investment in 
the region. The R498 is the most direct route from 
Nenagh to Thurles and Clonmel.  This scheme 
will serve to enhance this link by reducing journey 
times and improving road safety”. 
 
Tipperary County Council advises that Traffic 
Management will be in place from time to time for 
this project to ensure the flow of traffic, and will 
keep the public notified through regular 
communications on www.tipperarycoco.ie and on 
social media.

Speed Limit Review - 
update 
The Department of Transport carried out a Review of 
Speed Limits nationally and this has resulted in changes 
to the default speed limits for roads in Ireland. These 
changes were signed into law in April 2024.   The 
changes to the legislation will reduce the default speed 
limits on some road categories including:  
• 
60km/hr on Rural Local Roads (reduction 
from 80km/hr) 
• 
80km/hr on National Secondary Roads 
(currently 100km/hr) 
• 
30km/hr in Urban Areas (currently 
predominantly 50km/hr). 
 
The implementation of the reduction of a default speed 
limit on local roads to 60km/hr is complete. Tipperary 
County Council is awaiting feedback data from the 
RSA on the impact of this change. 
It is proposed by the National 
Group that implementation of the 
speed limits will be done in phases:  
• 
Phase 1 - Rural Local 
Roads (Complete) 
• 
Phase 2 - National 
Secondary Roads and 
Urban Areas  
• 
Phase 3 - Other Special 
Circumstances, such as 
schools.   
Progress on Phase 2 and 3 stalled 
for a number of months awaiting 
publication of national guidance 
documents. These documents were 
published in September 2025 and 
the review process will now 
commence in January 2026.

CFRAM FLOOD RELIEF SCHEMES 
 
Flood Relief Schemes 
Current Update 
Ballina FRS 
The first consultation with the public and stakeholders took 
place online from 8th November – 6th December 2021. The 
second public consultation day was held 12th June 2025 during 
which the community was presented with five options 
developed to alleviate flooding including the emerging preferred 
option.  
Significant requests for further information and amendments to 
the scheme were made by attendees.  The design team are 
currently undertaking a high-level review taking these 
submissions into consideration.  
Upon selection of the emerging preferred option, the scheme 
would then proceed to Stage II, the planning process, where the 
preferred option would be developed and an application would 
be submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála. 
Golden FRS 
The Golden FRS failed the Scheme Viability Review Report 
(SVR) which concluded that there is no potentially economical 
scheme that could be taken to full Flood Relief Scheme project 
stage. 
Tipperary County Council requested that the OPW reconsider 
this decision and allow the Golden Scheme progress through to 
Stage 1 Option Selection allowing a more detailed analysis of the 
options that can be undertaken, and more certainty be obtained 
in relation to the cost estimates. 
Holycross FRS 
Stage I Option Selection for Holycross FRS is complete. The 
proposed Capital Flood Relief Scheme was not accepted by the 
benefitting property owners. 
 
Knocklofty FRS 
In July 2024 the OPW approved the Preferred Option in the 
Options Report, which enabled progression of the Knocklofty 
FRS.  The Preferred Option is to construct raised defences on 
the River Suir to prevent flooding with stormwater drainage 
behind the defences. Total budget of €1.1m.  
This option was presented to the public for feedback on 17th 
April 2025 during the second Public Consultation Day for the 
scheme. The scheme received largely positive feedback and 
issues raised by the public have been taken into consideration.  
This project is currently in Stage II, the planning process, where 
the preferred option is being developed and an application will 
be submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála in 2026.

Flood Relief Schemes 
Current Update 
Marlfield Lake FRS 
The ground investigation for the scheme has commenced and is 
due to be completed early 2026. The results of the ground 
investigation will facilitate the Design Team in selecting the most 
appropriate design options for the Marlfield Flood Relief 
Scheme. Upon selection of the emerging preferred option, the 
scheme would then proceed to Stage II, the planning process, 
where the preferred option would be developed and an 
application would be submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála. 
 
In parallel with the Capital FRS in Marlfield, work is continuing 
with the interim dam rehabilitation protection works involving 
various measures that will protect the existing dam and the 
surrounding area. Undertaking work in Marlfield Lake area is 
complex with many environmental and statutory constraints, 
however we have been engaging with the relevant stakeholders 
and significant progress has been made. 
 
All of the above is subject to OPW funding and approval. 
Nenagh FRS 
The scope and complexity of the Nenagh Flood Relief Scheme 
has evolved significantly, and the scheme was formally 
reclassified in September 2023 from a ‘small project’ to a major 
flood relief scheme.  This decision reflects the scale of works 
required, the inclusion of critical infrastructure, and the need for 
robust governance and resources for a capital project of such 
magnitude. 
Preparatory work by the OPW has been ongoing with 
preliminary site surveys (topographical and CCTV) recently 
completed. A Steering Group has been established to oversee 
delivery of the Nenagh FRS. 
Tender documents for the procurement of consultants to 
progress both the engineering and environmental elements of 
the scheme are currently being prepared. 
Stage I – Option Identification & Preliminary Design will 
commence following the procurement and appointment of the 
Design Team.  This is expected to progress in 2026 subject to 
OPW approval.

Staff Department and Area 
•

•

Derelict Sites 
 
The Derelict Sites Act requires the owner of a building or land to ensure that they do not become or 
continue to be derelict. The Act defines a derelict site as being any land which detracts, or is likely to 
detract, to a material degree from the amenity, character or appearance of land in the 
neighbourhood.  
 
At the start of 2025 the derelict sites register contained 84 properties and the owners of these 
properties were issued with a letter reminding them of their obligations under the Act to carry out 
works to render the buildings non-derelict. To date we have removed 19 of these properties from the 
register as the works have been carried out. The latest register shows 115 properties with additional 
properties being added throughout the county. The team will maintain a focus on this in 2026 with a 
view towards adopting a systematic countywide approach to identifying derelict properties with an 
initial focus on the nine historic regional towns.  
 
The team have commenced two CPO processes and aim to increase the level of interaction with 
property owners to increase the awareness of the focus on vacancy and dereliction countywide.  
 
URDF Call 3 
URDF Call 3 seeks to tackle long term vacant and derelict buildings and sites across URDF towns and 
cities primarily in order to accelerate the provision of residential development and regenerate town 
centres.  An allocation of €5m has been approved for Tipperary County Council under this Call. 
There are 85 properties on the list divided between the URDF designated towns of Clonmel, Nenagh 
and Thurles. We are in the process of adding additional properties to the list as they are identified. To 
date approximately 60% of these properties are in the process of being brought back into use.
